question: Should the experimental grouped-Claw update planner, its versioned JSON contract, and capability-consent model be accepted as an OpenClaw core lifecycle surface rather than kept outside core or deferred pending the RFC/stack review?
rationale: The PR is technically substantial but introduces durable product and host-integration semantics across core config, state ownership, MCP, cron, and future mutation flows; code review cannot decide that ownership boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor the staged core lifecycle
options.body: Keep the feature gated in core, land the planning stage only after final-head proof, and review the downstream apply stage as a separate consent-sensitive change.

options.title: Defer pending RFC direction
options.body: Pause this stack until the RFC establishes the intended core scope, host contract, and long-term ownership model.

options.title: Move optional lifecycle tooling outward
options.body: Prefer a plugin or external workflow if maintainers do not want grouped package lifecycle and consent policy in OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the staged core lifecycle
recommendation.body: Keep the feature gated in core, land the planning stage only after final-head proof, and review the downstream apply stage as a separate consent-sensitive change.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned on the PR and authored the detailed review constraints for the lifecycle-planning contract.
